title: Who reports improper dispensing and serious adverse drug events, which events are reportable, and within what period
subtopic: Serious events: reporters, triggers and periods
rule_summary: Under 247 CMR 20.02(1), a Manager of Record of a pharmacy shall report to the Board any improper dispensing of a prescription drug that results in serious injury or death within seven business days of discovery of serious injury or death related to improper dispensing. Under 247 CMR 20.02(2), a Manager of Record of a pharmacy shall report any serious adverse drug event that occurs as a result of a patient's interaction with any drug or pharmaceutical manufactured, produced, or compounded at the pharmacy, to: (a) the Board; (b) the Federal Food and Drug Administration MedWatch Program; and (c) the Betsy Lehman Center for Patient Safety and Medical Error Reduction; a Manager of Record shall report a serious adverse drug event within seven business days of the knowledge of the serious adverse drug event by any pharmacy employee. Under M.G.L. c. 112, s. 39D(b), a pharmacy shall inform the department of public health of any improper dispensing of a prescription drug that results in serious injury or death, as defined by the department in regulations, as soon as is reasonably and practically possible, but not later than 7 business days after discovery of the improper dispensing. Under M.G.L. c. 112, s. 39D(c), the manager of record of a pharmacy shall report any serious adverse drug event, as defined in section 51H of chapter 111, occurring as a result of the patient's interaction with any drug or pharmaceutical manufactured, produced or compounded at the manager of record's pharmacy, to the board, the federal Food and Drug Administration MedWatch Program and the Betsy Lehman center for patient safety and medical error reduction, and this data shall be reported to the board within 7 business days of the knowledge of any serious adverse drug event by any pharmacy employee. On their terms, 247 CMR 20.02(1) and M.G.L. c. 112, s. 39D(b) reach improper dispensing only where it results in serious injury or death, and 247 CMR 20.02(2) and M.G.L. c. 112, s. 39D(c) reach a serious adverse drug event only where it occurs as a result of a patient's interaction with a drug or pharmaceutical manufactured, produced or compounded at the pharmacy.
exam_relevance: Tests who makes each report (a Manager of Record of the pharmacy under 247 CMR 20.02; the pharmacy and its manager of record under M.G.L. c. 112, s. 39D), that the improper-dispensing reports reach only improper dispensing that results in serious injury or death and the serious-adverse-drug-event reports only a drug or pharmaceutical manufactured, produced or compounded at the pharmacy, the recipients of each report, and the seven-business-day periods with their different starting events.

authority.name: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy reporting regulations

numeric_facts.fact: period for a Manager of Record's report to the Board of improper dispensing of a prescription drug that results in serious injury or death
numeric_facts.conditions: 247 CMR 20.02(1); from discovery of serious injury or death related to improper dispensing

numeric_facts.fact: period for a Manager of Record's report of a serious adverse drug event
numeric_facts.conditions: 247 CMR 20.02(2); from the knowledge of the serious adverse drug event by any pharmacy employee; a serious adverse drug event occurring as a result of a patient's interaction with a drug or pharmaceutical manufactured, produced or compounded at the pharmacy

numeric_facts.fact: outer limit for a pharmacy to inform the Department of Public Health of improper dispensing of a prescription drug that results in serious injury or death
numeric_facts.conditions: M.G.L. c. 112, s. 39D(b); as soon as is reasonably and practically possible, but not later than 7 business days after discovery of the improper dispensing

numeric_facts.fact: period for reporting a serious adverse drug event to the board under the statute
numeric_facts.conditions: M.G.L. c. 112, s. 39D(c); from the knowledge of any serious adverse drug event by any pharmacy employee

exceptions: The reporting requirements in 247 CMR 20.02 do not apply to non-resident pharmacies (247 CMR 20.02(5)).
common_confusions: Naming the pharmacist or pharmacy intern who dispensed or administered as the person who files, when 247 CMR 20.02(1) and (2) place the report on a Manager of Record of the pharmacy, and M.G.L. c. 112, s. 39D(b) and (c) place the corresponding duties on the pharmacy and its manager of record.
Treating every dispensing error as reportable, when 247 CMR 20.02(1) and M.G.L. c. 112, s. 39D(b) reach improper dispensing of a prescription drug that results in serious injury or death.

Treating every serious adverse drug event as reportable under these provisions, when 247 CMR 20.02(2) and M.G.L. c. 112, s. 39D(c) reach one occurring as a result of a patient's interaction with a drug or pharmaceutical manufactured, produced or compounded at the pharmacy.

Running every seven-business-day period from the same event: 247 CMR 20.02(1) runs from discovery of serious injury or death related to improper dispensing, M.G.L. c. 112, s. 39D(b) from discovery of the improper dispensing, and the serious adverse drug event report from the knowledge of the event by any pharmacy employee.

Sending every report to the Board alone, when M.G.L. c. 112, s. 39D(b) names the Department of Public Health and a serious adverse drug event report also goes to the Federal Food and Drug Administration MedWatch Program and the Betsy Lehman Center for Patient Safety and Medical Error Reduction.
